source.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
source.authors: Kevin Wang; Alexandre Variengien; Arthur Conmy; Buck Shlegeris; Jacob Steinhardt

record.tranche_reason: This is the original study. It uses its own head interventions and IOI measurements to identify and validate the circuit, including knockouts, path patching, and circuit criteria.
record.gate_note: The study reports several path-patching scans as figures. Where the text describes a scan but gives no exact value, the result is recorded qualitatively or as figure only. Head-level figure values used only to select heads are not separately transcribed. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: This is the original source (arXiv:2211.00593). It discovers and validates the 26-head IOI circuit in GPT-2 small using path patching, mean-ablation knockouts, and faithfulness/completeness/minimality tests. Because it is the original source, no verdict labels are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that they isolated a 26-head, 7-class IOI circuit in GPT-2 small. Their criteria support it, but it fails the hardest tests (greedy incompleteness), and backup heads compensate for knocked-out Name Movers. S-Inhibition attention, MLPs and layer norms remain poorly understood. A preliminary GPT-2 medium analysis suggests more complex behaviour there. Overall, they argue mechanistic understanding of large models looks feasible.
record.recipe_differences: This is the original study and method. It uses path patching, mean ablation, activation patching, and circuit-level faithfulness, completeness, and minimality tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that greedy completeness search finds large incompleteness scores, unlike random and whole-class subset sampling. IOI performance also changes on the additional-IO prompt distribution.
record.problems: The authors say they do not fully understand the S-Inhibition Heads, MLP and layer-normalization effects, or the cause of backup-head compensation. The greedy completeness sets are difficult to interpret. Some relevant results are shown in figures without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper includes additional per-head path-patching scans, attention-pattern analyses, and minimality scores in Figures 3, 5, 7, 12, 13, 15, 17, and 18. Exact per-head values are not stated in the text and were not transcribed as separate rows. The paper also reports signal-combination values in Figure 9; those were omitted because the main circuit-role patching result is summarized in r7.

untested.parts: Other model families, training checkpoints and a full circuit in GPT-2 medium are not tested. Task reuse is only hinted at (Appendix H, repeated random tokens).
Other circuit-finding methods are not compared. Zero ablation is only noted as 'noisy'.
No systematic comparison of ablation types (mean vs zero vs resample) or metrics on the circuit scores.
No per-template or per-order (ABBA vs BABA) mechanism breakdown, and no prompts with more than two names in the clause structure.
The origin of compensation (dropout is only hypothesised) and whether it occurs beyond IOI are untested.

missing.what: Name Mover, Backup and Negative heads write in the next-token direction on repeated random sequences; the authors say they are involved beyond IOI.
After Name Mover knockout, Negative Name Movers become less negative and 10.7 turns positive. Backup heads were chosen with a 2% effect threshold.
Signal-combination logit differences after patching S-Inhibition outputs: 3.55, 2.45, 1.77 / -0.99, -1.96, -3.16. Approximated as 2.31Spos+0.99Stok.
Per-head minimality F values and K sets for all 26 heads.
Longer prefixes with constant S1-S2 distance leave logit difference unchanged (3.56 vs 3.57).
Negative Name Mover negative copy score 98% vs 12% for an average head; Name Mover attention to IO 0.59.

record.verdict_notes: This is the original source for all versions, so no verdict labels are given. The reader's V3 'tested' rests only on the preliminary GPT-2 medium remark and Appendix H. V4 is not tested. The r15 naive-circuit faithfulness value (0.1) is inconsistent with the full circuit's 0.46 gap described as comparable; check against the published version.

versions.untested_parts: The study focuses on GPT-2 small and attention heads; it does not establish that its account captures all computation, including MLP and layer-normalization contributions.
The cause and generality of backup-head compensation are not established.

The GPT-2 medium analysis is preliminary; the study does not establish that the same full circuit and roles operate across other sizes, models, or training checkpoints, or that the components are reused for other tasks.
The study does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics to establish method independence.

The study tests its own mean-ablation setup and logit-difference completeness criteria; it does not systematically vary ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution to compare evaluation sensitivity.
The study uses templates and both ABBA/BABA name orders, and tests additional-name cases, but does not separately verify the proposed mechanism for every template, name order, or more-name format.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measured IOI performance on the generated pIOI distribution

conditions.value: pIOI; 15 templates, with ABBA and BABA patterns

rows.measure: Mean logit difference; proportion of examples with IO predicted over S; mean IO probability
rows.note: The study reports these as aggregate results over pIOI.
rows.check: This is a capability baseline (behaviour only). Aggregated over templates and ABBA/BABA, it cannot show whether the same mechanism operates per variant. Drop the V6 link or treat it as cannot_determine for V6.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Path-patched each head's direct path to the logits using pABC activations

conditions.value: pIOI input patched with corresponding pABC activation

rows.value: Heads 9.6, 9.9, and 10.0 had a large positive effect; heads 10.7 and 11.10 had a large negative effect
rows.note: The text identifies the heads and directions of effect, but does not give their exact effect sizes.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measured name-copying scores for the three Name Mover Heads using their OV matrices
rows.measure: Copy score: proportion of samples where the input name is in the top 5 logits
rows.baseline: Less than 20% for an average head
rows.value: Above 95% for each of the three Name Mover Heads
rows.note: This supports the stated name-copying role, not the completeness of the overall circuit.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Path-patched heads into the Name Mover Heads' query vectors
rows.value: Heads 7.3, 7.9, 8.6, and 8.10 cause a significant drop through this path
rows.note: The study identifies these as S-Inhibition Heads.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Patched all four S-Inhibition Heads' paths to Name Mover queries from pABC
rows.value: Patching increases attention to S1 and reduces attention to IO
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations shown in figure; values not stated
rows.note: The text describes this as evidence that S-Inhibition Heads produce selective attention to IO.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Path-patched candidate heads into S-Inhibition Heads' values
rows.value: Four heads had significant negative effects; two attended from S2 to S1 and two from S2 to S1+1
rows.note: The study characterizes the first pair as Duplicate Token Heads and the second as Induction Heads.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Patched Duplicate Token and Induction Head outputs from datasets with altered signals

conditions.value: Different S1 and S2 tokens but unchanged positions

rows.value: Position-signal patching caused a drop of at least 88% of the S-Inhibition effect; changing tokens at the same positions caused less than 8% of that drop
rows.note: The authors say the result supports these heads as the origin of the position signal.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Path-patched heads into Induction Heads' keys at S1+1
rows.value: Heads 4.11 and 2.2 caused a decrease in logit difference and were identified as Previous Token Heads
rows.note: The study also reports these heads have the highest previous-token score on repeated random-token sequences.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Knocked out all Name Mover Heads
rows.value: Only a 5% drop; the task still worked
rows.note: After knockout, the authors identified other heads that compensated for the removed Name Mover Heads.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Path-patched heads to the logits after knocking out Name Mover Heads

conditions.value: All Name Mover Heads knocked out

rows.value: Eight selected heads were called Backup Name Mover Heads; they compensate for loss of the main Name Mover Heads
rows.note: The backup heads have diverse pre-knockout behavior; the study says the cause and mechanism of compensation remain unclear.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Knocked out all attention heads outside the proposed circuit, defining the circuit function

conditions.value: The proposed circuit of attention heads

rows.value: The circuit achieves 87% of full-model performance; |F(M)-F(C)|=0.46
rows.note: The authors call this supportive of faithfulness but note remaining gaps.
rows.check: Faithfulness is 87% of F(M) (gap 0.46, 13%). The authors treat this as supportive. For V5 it shows the circuit explains only part of the logit difference. The state is fine.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuit and full-model performance after removing subsets of circuit nodes

conditions.value: Uniformly random subsets and whole head classes

rows.value: The authors report that every score from these two sampling strategies was small
rows.note: Exact scores are not stated in the text.
rows.check: This is only the random and class-based sampling condition. For V5 it is the contrast condition to r13, so pair it with r13.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Greedily searched for subsets of circuit nodes maximizing incompleteness
rows.value: Up to 3.09, reported as 87% of the original logit difference
rows.note: The greedily found sets were usually not semantically interpretable.
rows.check: Greedy incompleteness reaches up to 3.09 (87% of original). For V5 this fully shows that how complete the circuit looks depends on the search method. For V1's completeness criterion it is a failure, so if linked to V1 the state should be reversed/absent for the greedy condition rather than partial.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, lines 809–812; Section 4.1, lines 932–938; Appendix M.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Removed circuit nodes and tested whether restoring each node changed logit difference

conditions.value: All 26 heads in the proposed circuit

rows.value: Every head had a nontrivial impact, at least 1% of the original logit difference
rows.note: The authors also state that some individual head contributions are small.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated a naive circuit under the faithfulness criterion

conditions.value: Name Movers, S-Inhibition Heads, two Induction Heads, two Duplicate Token Heads, and Previous Token Heads; excludes Backup and Negative Name Mover Heads

rows.value: 0.1, described as comparable to the full circuit's faithfulness score
rows.note: The naive circuit is more easily shown incomplete by random or class-based knockouts; greedy search finds similarly large incompleteness scores for both circuits.
rows.check: This is a comparator (naive circuit), not the proposed circuit, so do not link it to V1. The reported 0.1 faithfulness conflicts with the full circuit's 0.46 gap, yet the text calls them 'comparable'. The value is ambiguous and should be flagged.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Knocked out MLP layers individually and, separately, all MLP layers after the first
rows.value: Knocking out MLP0 alone reverses the sign; knocking out all MLPs after the first gives -1.1; other layers individually have little effect
rows.note: The proposed circuit contains attention heads, and the authors leave a more precise investigation of MLP roles for future work.
rows.check: MLP knockouts (MLP0 reverses sign; all MLPs after the first give -1.1) show that the attention-head circuit is not the whole story. The baseline 3.56 should be stated. The link to V1 is weak, since V1 names heads only.

rows.subject: GPT-2 medium
rows.operation_detail: Preliminary analysis of heads directly influencing IOI logits
rows.measure: Direct influence on logits and attention to IO and S
rows.value: A sparse set of heads directly influenced the logits, but not all of these heads attended to IO and S
rows.note: The study does not report a complete GPT-2 medium circuit or establish the same roles as GPT-2 small.
rows.check: This is a preliminary GPT-2 medium result. Its name-mover-like heads don't all attend to IO/S. No numbers are given.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the IOI task with an additional occurrence of S in a natural sentence

conditions.value: S appears three times in total and IO once

rows.measure: Logit difference; IO probability; proportion with S logit greater than IO
rows.note: This is the study's control dataset for the additional-IO adversarial condition.
rows.check: This is a control prompt variant (extra S). Behaviour holds (3.64 vs 3.55), but it is a behavioural measure only, with no check of the mechanism.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated IOI prompts with an additional occurrence of IO in a natural sentence

conditions.value: Both S and IO tokens are duplicated; additional natural sentence contains IO

rows.measure: Logit difference; IO probability; proportion with S logit greater than IO
rows.note: The authors report that the adversarial distribution significantly reduces logit difference and increases S-over-IO predictions.
rows.check: With duplicated IO, behaviour degrades (logit difference 1.23, 23.4% S>IO), and S-Inhibition heads also attend to the second IO. This is a prompt format the circuit's heuristic mishandles. The V5 link is weak (this is prompt-distribution dependence of behaviour, not of the circuit evaluation), so keep V6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Section 4, lines 809–812; Section 4.1, lines 932–938; Appendix M.

relation.reason: Direct interventions and circuit evaluations test the proposed IOI mechanism.

tranche.reason: Original study establishing the circuit and its intervention methods and evaluation measures.

source_check.notes: Knockouts use pABC mean activations computed within templates, with circuit nodes defined at head/token positions; MLPs and layer norms remain in the computation. Minimality is conditional on removed subsets, and greedy search exposes substantial incompleteness; statements about other studies were assessed only for their claims about this source.
